messages:
maya: Heads-up — APAC-2 reported heavy GPU queueing after the regional drain started. Latency up, some requests timing out. DNS steering shows a lot of clients still resolving to apac-1.

eric: Yep seeing the same. apac-2 capacity down to ~30% available because of the maintenance window + a burst from long-running evals.

raj: Do we have TTLs on the apac A records? Might be why traffic is stuck on apac-1 or still bouncing.

maya: TTL was intentionally long (900s) to stabilize during last rollout. Thought we primed caches earlier but looks like edge caches held it.

ops-oncall: Quick checklist: reduce TTL, prime region DNS, start weighted traffic shift, then drain GPUs. We should avoid full cutover.

maya: Agreed. Proposed steps: 1) lower TTL to 60s on steering records; 2) push a short-lived CNAME for apac-2 to absorb new resolves; 3) pre-warm apac-2 model caches with canary traffic; 4) do a 10% increment shift every 2m.

eric: Sounds good. I'm on the DNS change. Changing TTL now (doing it via infra-dns).

sre-bot: Deploy triggered: infra-dns/chg/2113456792 by eric (ttl update apac steering -> 60s).

raj: After TTL change, we should run some dig checks from multiple regions. If resolvers still return old RR due to stub cache, we might need to nudge via resolver prefetch or ask CDN partner.

maya: Can someone post a few dig outputs? I want to verify apac-2 addresses appear.

eric: From cloud-runner in us-west: `dig +short apac-steer.redwood.internal` -> `10.2.1.45` (apac-1), `10.2.2.10` (apac-2) — both present, apac-1 first.

raj: From edge-probe asia-east: `dig apac-steer` -> still only apac-1. Likely resolver TTL/negative caching. Edge cache still serving old answer.

maya: OK. We'll prime apac-2 by sending a stream of short inference requests with model warmup to populate KV caches. eric, can you bump weighted traffic to 5% now? We want to see error rate and latency at small scale.

eric: Bumping to 5% now via traffic-router: `trafficctl set-weight apac-2 5`

ops-oncall: Observing metrics: apac-2 incoming qps increased, GPU memory warmed, latency ~15% higher but stable. No failures so far.

maya: Good. Continue priming for 4m then increase to 20%.

raj: Note — some customers (enterprise private) have pinned A records internally; their resolvers won't respect steer changes. We should list impacted customers and reach out if critical.

eric: Also logged a ticket with CDN partner for resolver flush on their POPs — some POPs still hold the 900s. Ticket 13821.

maya: On the DNS side: after lowering TTL, full convergence still may take up to previous TTL for certain resolvers. So the staged traffic shift is the safe path.

ops-oncall: Small gotcha — when we reduce TTL, it doesn't flush existing cached answers. It only affects new caches. That's why priming + canary weight is crucial.

maya: Action items: eric set TTL -> done. eric ramp weight 5% -> done. raj coordinate CDN ticket and customer pin list. ops-oncall continue health checks and call out anomalies. I'll manage the GPU drain schedule and report back every 5m.

eric: Noted. Starting 5% -> 20% ramp in 4m if no errors.

sre-bot: Incident note appended: apac steering TTL reduced, staged traffic shift initiated, priming underway.

maya: Update in 10m: apac-2 handling 22% of new resolves, GPUs warmed, tail latency improved after warmup. We can continue to 50% next if metrics hold.

ops-oncall: Keep an eye on token-level cost — priming lots of warmup calls increases cost. If we hit cost threshold, pause and use short synthetic warmups instead.

raj: Reminder to revert TTL to normal after steady state (900s) to reduce DNS churn. We'll schedule that post-drain.

maya: Thanks all. We'll keep this thread for the next hour while we finish the drain and confirm DNS convergence.
